Ford, a big car company, recently announced it was cutting 800 jobs in the UK. At the same time, they criticized government rules that require car companies to sell more electric vehicles every year. They called these rules "unworkable." However, back in 2022, Ford actually supported these same rules and even wanted the targets to be set higher. The figure they pushed for was even stricter than what the government originally proposed. This group of car companies, including Ford, were singing a very different tune back then, essentially asking for tougher electric vehicle sales goals.

female readers and general audiences should know that this dramatic change in Ford's position shows how the car industry miscalculated the situation. During the COVID-19 pandemic, when interest rates were very low, car companies could sell every vehicle they produced. The operation of selling cars was easy, and profits were like low-hanging fruit — simple to grab. But now, demand for electric cars has slowed down significantly, and companies like Ford are struggling to meet the sales targets they once championed.

So in short, Ford is now complaining about rules that they themselves once pushed for. The figure of 800 job cuts is partly a result of this difficult situation the industry finds itself in. It's a bit like a group of people who demanded a strict diet plan and are now upset that the fruit and vegetables on the menu are too hard to eat. The article uses Ford's operation as an example of how the whole industry failed to sing the same song consistently when it comes to electric vehicle planning.

P.P.S This article highlights how business priorities can shift dramatically when market conditions change, leaving companies in contradictory positions regarding policies they once strongly supported.
